Both updated successfully.

Summary of what I learned and saved:

The error: my answer -10295.54 vs gold -156.11 (~66x too big). Reverse-engineering showed -10,295 ≈ 10% of the ~$100B Federal Reserve notes level = a full-YEAR change during late-1970s ~10%/yr inflation. So I almost certainly read two cells 12 months apart (a year-over-year pair) or a YTD/cumulative cell, instead of the two ADJACENT May 1979 and June 1979 month-end values that a "month-over-month" question requires.

Two generalizable lessons recorded (skill patch + memory):

1. Month-over-month CPI-adjusted change: use the ADJACENT-month CPI ratio (e.g. CPI Jun/May ≈ 1.0074, not a YoY ratio). The real MoM change is tiny relative to the level because one month of inflation nearly cancels the small nominal change — so the gold is a small signed number. Diagnostic: a "month-over-month" answer that comes out ~10-66x too big and ≈ an annual-magnitude change means you grabbed the wrong period (12 months apart or a YTD cell).

2. "Federal Reserve notes" is a named COMPONENT row — read it as named. This is the opposite of the existing "TOTAL currency in circulation = grand total" trap. Disambiguated both in the skill so future runs read the grand total only when the question says "TOTAL."

Done.
